observations.explanation: The paper reports SWE-agent results alongside both interactive Shell-only and retrieval-augmented (RAG) baselines, including 12.47% resolved on the full test set and 18.00% on Lite for GPT-4 Turbo (PDF pp. 5–6). This supports the stated benchmark-performance comparison.

The ablations compare the editor configuration with Shell-only editing and compare linting against no linting; the paper reports lower resolution without the editor and a 3-point decrease without linting (PDF pp. 6–7). This supports the claim that these interface elements contribute to measured performance.

The paper states that its results, ablations, and analysis are based on GPT-4 Turbo and Claude 3 Opus, and says additional models such as Llama 3 and DeepSeek Coder performed subpar in the agent setting (PDF p. 5). The stated scope limitation is grounded in the paper.

The paper says the final ACI design was reached through qualitative analysis on a small set of hand-picked, easier development examples, while reporting evaluation on SWE-bench (PDF p. 5). This reasonably leaves generalization beyond those design choices and benchmark conditions open; the claim is framed as an uncertainty, not as a demonstrated defect.
